sections.heading: The idea
sections.body_md:
A unit step is the running integral of a unit impulse. Once the impulse has occurred, the step holds the value 1. Linearity moves that identity from the input to the output: the step response is the running integral of the impulse response. For a causal system the integral starts at time 0, because the impulse response is zero before the impulse.

A pulse is two steps. A pulse of height \(A\) that turns on at time 0 and turns off at time \(T\) is a step of height \(A\) at time 0 minus a step of height \(A\) at time \(T\). Until time \(T\) the second step has not started, so the output is only the response to the first step. After time \(T\) both steps contribute, and the second one is delayed by \(T\).

sections.heading: Key equations
sections.body_md:
\[
y_{\mathrm{step}}(t)=\int_0^t h(\lambda)\,d\lambda
\]
\[
u_{\mathrm{pulse}}(t)=A\,u(t)-A\,u(t-T)
\]
The output follows the same difference, with the unit-step response in place of \(u\). The area of a pulse is its height times its width, and that area is the weight of the impulse that matches a very short pulse.

sections.heading: Worked example
sections.body_md: Take the causal impulse response \(h(t)=22e^{-8t}\). Its area is \(22/8=2.75\), so the unit-step response settles at 2.75. A separate pulse of height 9 that lasts 0.7 s has area \(9\times 0.7=6.3\). That pulse is a step of height 9 minus a step of height 9 that begins at 0.7 s. At \(t=0.3\ \mathrm{s}\), which is still inside the pulse, the delayed step contributes nothing, and the output is the response to the step of height 9 alone.

sections.heading: Common pitfalls
sections.body_md: Integrating the impulse response from the far future back toward the impulse, instead of from 0 up to the time of interest. Subtracting the delayed step during the pulse, before that step exists. Reading a pulse's area from its height and forgetting the width.

sections.heading: Where this leads
sections.body_md: The exponential shape of a single real pole, including how far a step has risen after one time constant, is the first-order skill. A circuit then uses the same pulse, built as a difference of steps, when the memory is a capacitor.
